extracted.intended_audience: Department of Indian Affairs officials, Indian agents, and members of Congress / policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards used by the Commissioner to assess tribes' advancement toward self-support and 'civilization', to recommend legislative or administrative actions (land confirmation, removals, appropriations, allotments, agency changes), and to evaluate agency performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: School attendance / education
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether children attend boarding- or day-schools (example: 'The two boarding-schools have been attended by 308 pupils' ; 'They are averse to schools and prefer to instruct their children in their own language').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: School enrollment numbers are treated as indicators of progress; reluctance or refusal to send children to school is cited as an impediment to adjustment. The report contrasts tribes attending school and wearing citizens' dress with those 'still wearing their blankets and living in tepees.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of citizens' dress and housing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of 'citizens' dress' and living in houses rather than tepees or blankets (e.g., 'Nearly all at White Earth wear citizen's dress, live in houses').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wearing citizens' dress and occupying houses is presented as a visible marker of 'advancement in industry and thrift' and of approaching parity with white settlements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement in remunerative labor / industry
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation in paid labor such as freighting, brick-making, burning lime, hauling stone, farming, stock-raising (e.g., 'engage in every kind of remunerative labor which the agent can furnish them—freighting, making brick, burning lime, hauling stone').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Willingness to undertake such work and the presence of demand (often exceeding supply) are signs of industriousness; agents' ability to furnish such employment and the tribe's uptake are used to evaluate progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crop production and farm yields
rubrics_metrics.description: Measured agricultural output and acreage cultivated (examples: '9,540 bushels of corn have been raised from 1,180 acres'; 'They have raised this year 35,000 bushels of wheat, 3,200 bushels of oats and barley, and 5,000 bushels of vegetables').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crop yields and acres under cultivation are used as quantitative metrics of self-support and agricultural progress; poor yields due to drought are cited as reasons farming may not be reasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability of land / environmental constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: The agricultural prospects determined by land quality and climate (e.g., 'Self-support by farming cannot reasonably be expected of this generation of Indians in a country so liable to drought').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drought-prone or timbered lands that are expensive to clear are flagged as poor for farming; such environmental constraints inform recommendations to promote alternative industries (e.g., stock-raising) or relocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security of land title / legal confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether tribal land title is legally secure (e.g., 'A great drawback to energetic farming ... is the uncertain status of their land title. Until the tract which they now occupy is confirmed to them by act of Congress, they will be slow to settle down and make permanent improvements thereon').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal confirmation of title (act of Congress, purchase, patents with restrictions) is treated as prerequisite for permanent improvements, settlement, and willingness to invest labor and capital.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of tools, teams, and start-up assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Need for material assistance to enable farming or removal ('we also wish to settle ... requesting the aid of the government in obtaining teams, wagons, harness, tools, &c., with which to work our land').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report records petitions and recommendations that material supplies (teams, wagons, houses, cattle, seed, implements) be provided or appropriated to enable successful settlement or removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriations and targeted assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability and use of appropriated funds for assisting Indians in building houses, procuring seeds, implements, stock, or cash (example: US to appropriate annually $30,000 for 25 years to assist Crows).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The terms, amount, and duration of appropriations (and whether funds are to be expended under presidential direction) are treated as central to successful transitions like allotment and settlement; congressionally provided start-up support is repeatedly recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allotment in severalty and patent terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Allotting reservation lands in severalty with patents (often 'with restrictive clauses against alienation') and proposed acreages per head (example: 'allotted in severalty ... patents, with restrictive clauses against alienation').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allotment is presented as a mechanism to encourage individual cultivation and citizenship, but with protective restrictions; the report recommends preparing laws and bills to implement allotments and patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resistance to enrollment / pay-roll requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Willingness to be enrolled on new payroll forms and to submit accurate census data (e.g., 'They have refused to receive their annuities, owing to an objection ... to signing a new form of pay-roll').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refusal to be enrolled prevents accurate census and complicates annuity distribution and claims adjustment; enrollment is portrayed as necessary to adjust payments fairly and to administer benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of annuity/payment policy on labor incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: How cash annuity payments influence industriousness (e.g., 'Their cash annuity payment is a great obstacle to their advancement' because it reduces inclination to labor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report links annuity policy to productive behavior and suggests conditions (performing labor equal to annuity) or withholding payments until compliance to encourage work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proximity to whites / access to liquor and negative influences
rubrics_metrics.description: The tribe's proximity to white settlements and access to intoxicating liquors as a factor in demoralization (e.g., 'could at all times easily procure intoxicating liquors ... a large proportion of the tribe formed habits of dissipation').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Close contact with whites and liquor supply are treated as corrosive to progress; removal or relocation away from such contact is proposed as remedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social stability and leadership compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The effect of chiefs and internal leadership on compliance and progress (examples: Little Chief refusing schools; deposing of Chief Maw-mew-wah-ne-kah for impeding treaty execution; chiefs assuring agent they are satisfied and do not desire to return).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong leadership alignment with policy and tribal consent (or lack thereof) significantly affect outcomes; petitions and signatures by chiefs are used as evidence of consent to actions like relinquishing Dakota land.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to relocate / suitability of relocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Tribal consent and practicality of moving to better reservations (e.g., recommendations to remove some Chippewas to White Earth; Poncas' petition to visit Washington to sign away Dakota land and obtain title to current reservation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removal is endorsed where reservations offer better resources and isolation from harmful influences, often contingent on appropriations to defray removal and start-up costs; prior consent and incentives increase chance of success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency infrastructure and administration adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Condition of agency buildings, need for new ones, and adequacy of agency management ('There are no buildings at the agency fit to be used for agency purposes ... new ones are immediately required').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper agency facilities and competent agents are essential to protect public property, shelter employees, guard against outbreaks, and administer services; recommendations include building new structures or discontinuing ineffective agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security measures and military coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of disarming, dismounting, guarding, and military presence to protect reservation and prevent raids (e.g., 'recommended the disarming and dismounting of these Indians, and that sufficient supplies be furnished them ... and that they be properly guarded').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where hostile actors or outlaws threaten reservation peace, coordinated military action and security measures are presented as legitimate and necessary preconditions for stable administration and settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicators of successful 'civilization' (aggregated markers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Composite markers used repeatedly as evidence of progress: wearing citizens' dress, living in houses, attending school and church, cultivating specified acreage, owning implements and stock, building churches and houses, owning sewing-machines, mowing/reaping machines, plows, and producing quantifiable crop yields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report treats these aggregated, observable indicators as the primary evidence of peaceful policy success (example: Yakama Agency's data on dress, houses, acres cultivated, implements, and crop yields are cited as 'a good illustration of the practical results of the peace policy').

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic self-sufficiency versus dependence on government rations
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which a tribe requires government rations versus small issues or none (e.g., 'Self-support might have been attained ... but for their proximity to ... wild Kiowas and Comanches' ; 'require but small issues of rations').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduced dependence on rations and ability to support families through labor and farming are treated as milestones; continued dependence signals lack of advance and may justify policy interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of sale proceeds and investment for tribal benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: Disposition of proceeds from sale of reserve lands or discontinuance of agency (e.g., 'appraisement and sale of the lands included in the reserve, the proceeds of the sale to be invested for the benefit of the Indians').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When recommending sale or discontinuance of an agency, the report specifies that proceeds should be invested for the Indians' benefit as a fiduciary measure to support their welfare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely legislative action as prerequisite to settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Need for Acts of Congress or new laws to settle location, confirm titles, ratify agreements, and make appropriations (examples throughout: purchase from Cherokees, bills H.R. 6227 and S. 1760, need for new bill after boundary change).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many administrative recommendations are conditional on Congressional enactment; the report urges calling attention to Congress and preparing bills to authorize allotment, cession acceptance, and appropriations.
